claim: In LIHC patients (n=363), there is a positive correlation between the expression of NK-cell-associated genes (NCR1, KLRB1, CD160, PRF1, etc.) and PRDM1 expression.
source: Examination of 363 liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) patient samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) revealed a positive correlation between the expression of NK-cell-associated genes (Cursons et al., 2019) (NCR1, KLRB1, CD160, PRF1, etc.) and PRDM1 expression (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of TCGA patient data shown in Figure 1A, which displays correlation between NK gene expression and PRDM1.

claim: LIHC patients with higher NK-PRDM1 expression (above the median) have better survival outcomes compared to those with lower expression (below the median).
source: Notably, patients exhibiting higher levels of NK-PRDM1 expression (above the median) experienced better survival outcomes compared to those with lower levels of NK-PRDM1 expression (below the median; Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by survival analysis data from TCGA LIHC patients shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Similar positive correlations between NK-PRDM1 expression and survival were found in SKCM (n=454) and LUAD (n=497) patients.
source: Similar results were also found in skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM, n=454) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD, n=497) patients (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of TCGA data for SKCM and LUAD patients shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Patients in the highest quartile of NK-PRDM1 signature expression demonstrated enhanced overall survival in LUAD and SKCM patients with statistical significance.
source: Patients within the highest quartile of NK-PRDM1 signature expression demonstrated enhanced overall survival, a result that achieved statistical significance in LUAD and SKCM patients (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G-I).
evidence: The claim is supported by quartile-based survival analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G-I.

claim: PRDM1 in NK cells is essential for immune surveillance in solid tumors, including liver cancer.
source: These data suggested that PRDM1 in NK cells might be essential for immune surveillance in solid tumors, including liver cancer, and prompted us to investigate the function and mechanism of PRDM1 in NK cells and ILC1 within the context of liver cancer.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation and survival data presented for multiple cancer types.

claim: Ncr1-Cre mice were crossed with Prdm1fl/fl mice to generate Ncr1-cre Prdm1fl/fl mice, which specifically knockout exons 6–8 of Prdm1 in NKp46-positive cells.
source: Ncr1-Cre mice were crossed with Prdm1fl/fl mice to generate Ncr1-cre Prdm1fl/fl mice, which specifically knockout exons 6–8 of Prdm1 (Shapiro-Shelef et al., 2003) in NKp46-positive cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental mouse model generation with citation to the Prdm1 floxed allele design.

claim: The expression of Prdm1 was almost undetectable in CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+ cells of Prdm1 cko mice.
source: The expression of Prdm1 was almost undetectable in CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+ cells of Prdm1 cko mice, while was similar between total splenocytes in Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 1, E and F) indicating successful, and specifical knockout of Prdm1 in NKp46+ cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E and F demonstrating specific knockout in NKp46+ cells.

claim: The percentage and absolute number of NK cells (CD45+CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+) among lymphocytes was decreased in blood, lung, liver, spleen, and lymph nodes in Prdm1 cko mice compared with Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, the percentage and absolute number of NK cells (CD45+CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+) among lymphocytes was decreased in all of these tissues, whereas increased number of NK cells were observed in bone marrow (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Increased number of NK cells were observed in bone marrow of Prdm1 cko mice compared with Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, the percentage and absolute number of NK cells (CD45+CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+) among lymphocytes was decreased in all of these tissues, whereas increased number of NK cells were observed in bone marrow (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Stage IV (CD11b+CD27-) NK cells show higher level of effector molecules than any other stages and are considered as the most mature NK cells.
source: Stage IV (CD11b+CD27-) NK cells show higher level of effector molecules than any other stages and are considered as the most mature NK cells (Chiossone et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chiossone et al., 2009.

claim: The proportion of the most mature CD11b+CD27- NK cells were significantly decreased in blood, bone marrow, lung, liver, spleen, and lymph nodes in Prdm1 cko mice compared with Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, the proportion of the most mature CD11b+CD27- NK cells were significantly decreased in all of the analyzed tissues in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 1H; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data analyzing NK cell maturation stages shown in Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: A significant loss of KLRG1+ cells in NK cells was observed in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Consistent with CD11b/CD27 based maturation analysis, a significant loss of KLRG1+ cells in NK cells was observed in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Prdm1 is required for the terminal maturation of NK cells among various tissues.
source: Together, these data confirmed that Prdm1 is required for the terminal maturation of NK cells among various tissues.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the maturation marker data (CD11b/CD27 and KLRG1) across multiple tissues.

claim: Prdm1 cko mice exhibited an increased percentage of cNK cells (CD49a-CD49b+) and reduced proportion of ILC1s (CD49a+CD49b-) compared with Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, the Prdm1 cko mice exhibited an increased percentage of cNK cells (CD49a-CD49b+) and reduced proportion of ILC1s (CD49a+CD49b-) (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A analyzing liver group 1 ILC subpopulations.

claim: The absolute number of both cNK cells and ILC1s were decreased in Prdm1 cko mice, with a more robustly reduction in ILC1s.
source: Of note, the absolute number of both cNK cells and ILC1s were decreased in Prdm1 cko mice, with a more robustly reduction in ILC1s (Figure 2A), which underscored the crucial role of Prdm1 in maintaining the quantity of both liver cNK cells and ILC1s.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A quantifying absolute cell numbers.

claim: Prdm1 plays a crucial role in maintaining the quantity of both liver cNK cells and ILC1s.
source: Of note, the absolute number of both cNK cells and ILC1s were decreased in Prdm1 cko mice, with a more robustly reduction in ILC1s (Figure 2A), which underscored the crucial role of Prdm1 in maintaining the quantity of both liver cNK cells and ILC1s.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the observed reduction in absolute cell numbers in Prdm1 cko mice.

claim: Expression level of CD49b was slightly upregulated in Prdm1 cko cNK cells and NKp46+ cells in the liver and other tissues.
source: Expression level of CD49b was slightly upregulated in Prdm1 cko cNK cells and NKp46+ cells in the liver and other tissues (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: Increased CD49a expression was observed in Prdm1 cko liver ILC1s.
source: Increased CD49a expression was also observed in Prdm1 cko liver ILC1s, while it showed decreased expression in NKp46+ cells in the liver, bone marrow, and lymph nodes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F and G.

claim: Prdm1 is essential for maintaining the balance and hemostasis of cNK cells and ILC1s.
source: These results indicated the essential role of Prdm1 in maintaining the balance and hemostasis of cNK cells and ILC1s.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the observed changes in CD49a and CD49b expression and cell proportions.

claim: No significant difference in the in vivo cytotoxicity assay were observed between Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Although significant impaired homeostasis and maturation of NK cells were observed in Prdm1 cko mice, no significant difference in the in vivo cytotoxicity assay were observed between Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by B2M-deficient cell rejection assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2H and I.

claim: Deficiency of Prdm1 resulted in more metastasis nodules in both lung (~twofold) and liver (~fourfold) compared with Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, deficiency of Prdm1 resulted in more metastasis nodules in both lung (~twofold) and liver (~fourfold) (Figure 2B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by B16F10 tumor metastasis data shown in Figure 2B and D.

claim: Histological analysis confirmed the increased frequency of metastasis tumor foci in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Histological analysis further confirmed the increased frequency of metastasis tumor foci in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 2C and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining of liver and lung tissues shown in Figure 2C and E.

claim: Decreased IFN-γ secretion was observed in Prdm1 cko mice-derived splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells, and liver ILC1s when stimulated by IL-18 alone or IL-12/IL-18.
source: In agreement with the in vivo data, we also observed decreased IFN-γ secretion in Prdm1 cko mice-derived splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells, and liver ILC1s when stimulated by IL-18 alone or IL-12/IL-18 (Figure 2F; Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), which indicated that Prdm1 is required for full activation of cNK cells and ILC1s in the context of IFN-γ production.
evidence: The claim is supported by intracellular IFN-γ staining data shown in Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Prdm1 is required for full activation of cNK cells and ILC1s in the context of IFN-γ production.
source: In agreement with the in vivo data, we also observed decreased IFN-γ secretion in Prdm1 cko mice-derived splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells, and liver ILC1s when stimulated by IL-18 alone or IL-12/IL-18 (Figure 2F; Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), which indicated that Prdm1 is required for full activation of cNK cells and ILC1s in the context of IFN-γ production.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the observed decrease in IFN-γ production in Prdm1 cko cells.

claim: Prdm1 is indispensable for NK-cell-mediated tumor surveillance.
source: These data implied that Prdm1 is indispensable for NK-cell-mediated tumor surveillance.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the increased tumor metastasis and decreased IFN-γ production in Prdm1 cko mice.

claim: 445 DEGs were identified out of 17434 protein-coding genes in bulk RNA-seq of splenic cNK cells, consisting of 223 upregulated genes and 222 downregulated genes.
source: Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko mice were determined using a criterion of log2 (fold change)>0.5 and p<0.05. 445 DEGs were identified out of 17434 protein-coding genes, which consisted of 223 upregulated genes and 222 downregulated genes (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by bulk RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: GO analysis revealed the enrichment of glucuronate metabolism and lymphocyte differentiation in upregulated genes in Prdm1 cko mice derived NK cells.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis revealed the enrichment of glucuronate metabolism and lymphocyte differentiation in upregulated genes in Prdm1 cko mice derived NK cells (Figure 3C), both of which were associated with cellular growth and development.
evidence: The claim is supported by GO analysis of bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Leukocyte-mediated cytotoxicity, immune receptor activity, and integrin binding were enriched in the genes which decreased their expression level in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: In contrast, leukocyte-mediated cytotoxicity, immune receptor activity, and integrin binding were enriched in the genes which decreased their expression level in in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by GO analysis of bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: GSEA showed that NF-kappa B signaling pathway enriched in Prdm1-deficient cNK cells.
source: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) showed that NF-kappa B signaling pathway enriched in Prdm1-deficient cNK cells (Figure 3D), suggesting the potential targets by Prdm1 to regulate NK cell function.
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA of bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Increased expression of multiple TFs such as Junb, Batf3, Nfkb1, Tcf7, and Nr4a2 was observed in Prdm1 cko cNK cells.
source: Increased expression of multiple TFs such as Junb, Batf3, Nfkb1, Tcf7, and Nr4a2 was observed in Prdm1 cko cNK cells, suggesting they might be suppressed by Prdm1 (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Downregulation of granzyme B (Gzmb), Perforin (Prf1) were observed in Prdm1-deficient NK cells.
source: Downregulation of granzyme B (Gzmb), Perforin (Prf1) were observed in Prdm1-deficient NK cells (Figure 3E), implying decreased anti-tumor ability, which was consistent with increased melanoma metastasis in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 2, B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Decreased expression of Il18rap and Il12rb2 were observed in Prdm1 cko cNK cells.
source: Consistent with decreased production of IFN-γ after stimulated by IL-12/IL-18 (Figure 2F), decreased expression of Il18rap and Il12rb2 were observed in Prdm1 cko cNK cells (Figure 3E), implying impaired response to cytokine stimulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The percentage of CX3CR1+ cNK cells was significantly decreased in multiple tissues of Prdm1 cko mice.
source: The percentage of CX3CR1+ cNK cells was significantly decreased in multiple tissues of Prdm1 cko mice, while the proportion of CX3CR1+ ILC1 was increased in the liver (Figure 3, F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: The proportion of CX3CR1+ ILC1 was increased in the liver of Prdm1 cko mice.
source: The percentage of CX3CR1+ cNK cells was significantly decreased in multiple tissues of Prdm1 cko mice, while the proportion of CX3CR1+ ILC1 was increased in the liver (Figure 3, F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Lower GZMB and PRF1 production was observed in Prdm1-deficient splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells and ILC1s.
source: Lower GZMB and PRF1 production was observed in Prdm1-deficient splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells and ILC1s (Figure 3, H-K; Figure 3—figure supplement 1, A-I).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3H-K and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-I.

claim: The proportion of GZMB+ and PRF1+ cNK cells was decreased among almost all of the maturation stages of cNK cells.
source: Notably, the proportion of GZMB+ and PRF1+ cNK cells was decreased among almost all of the maturation stages of cNK cells (Figure 3, J and K).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data analyzing cytotoxic molecule expression across maturation stages shown in Figure 3J and K.

claim: Prdm1 may directly influence cytotoxic molecule in NK cells, rather than impacting their anti-tumor abilities solely by affecting the maturation phenotype of Prdm1-deficient NK cells.
source: These findings suggest that Prdm1 may directly influence cytotoxic molecule in NK cells, rather than impacting their anti-tumor abilities solely by affecting the maturation phenotype of Prdm1-deficient NK cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that cytotoxic molecules are reduced across all maturation stages, not just in immature cells.

claim: 10,978 cells passed the quality criteria and were selected for further scRNA-seq analysis (6,161 from Prdm1+/+ mice, 4,817 from Prdm1 cko mice).
source: 10,978 cells passed the quality criteria and were selected for further analysis (6,161 from Prdm1+/+ mice, 4,817 from Prdm1 cko mice).
evidence: The claim describes the quality control results for scRNA-seq data.

claim: Unsupervised clustering of all sequenced cells identified twelve distinct clusters, including B cells, epithelial cells (ECs), CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, NKT cells, ILC1s, cNK cells, dendritic cells (DCs), monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs), Monocytes, Kupffer cells (KCs), Neutrophils, and a small number of undefined cells.
source: Unsupervised clustering of all sequenced cells based on transcript signatures identified twelve distinct clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), including B cells, epithelial cells (ECs), CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, NKT cells, ILC1s, cNK cells, dendritic cells (DCs), monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs), Monocytes, Kupffer cells (KCs), Neutrophils, and a small number of undefined cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq clustering analysis shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In Prdm1 cko mice, an increased proportion of MDMs, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, Monocytes, and DCs was observed, alongside a decreased proportion of ECs, cNK cells, ILC1s, and NKT cells.
source: In Prdm1 cko mice, an increased proportion of MDMs, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, Monocytes, and DCs was observed, alongside a decreased proportion of ECs, cNK cells, ILC1s, and NKT cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data showing cell population changes in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: cNK cells expressed high levels of Itga2 (CD49b) and Eomes, while ILC1s had high levels expression of Itga1 (CD49a) and Tnfsf10.
source: cNK cells expressed high levels of Itga2 (CD49b) and Eomes, while ILC1s had high levels expression of Itga1 (CD49a) and Tnfsf10 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: Both cNK cells and ILC1s have significant reduced proportion in Prdm1 cko mouse.
source: Consistent with our flow cytometry data, both cNK cells and ILC1s have significant reduced proportion in Prdm1 cko mouse (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: In group 1 ILCs from Prdm1 cko mice, there was an increase in the proportion of cNK cells accompanied by a decrease in ILC1s.
source: In group 1 ILCs from Prdm1 cko mice, there was an increase in the proportion of cNK cells accompanied by a decrease in ILC1s (Figure 4, B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The subpopulation of liver cNK cells were referred as 'Prf1 high', 'Junb high', and 'Cxcr3 high' cNK cells.
source: Based on the cluster specific gene expression signature (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A), the subpopulation of liver cNK cells were referred as 'Prf1 high', 'Junb high', and 'Cxcr3 high' cNK cells (Figure 4D), with different distribution in Prdm1 cko and Prdm1+/+ genotype mice (Figure 4F; Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim describes the naming of cNK cell subclusters based on gene expression signatures shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The Prf1 high cNK cell cluster was defined by high expression of cytolysis-related genes, including Ncr1, Gzma, Gzmb, Prf1, and Fgl2.
source: The Prf1 high cNK cell cluster was defined by high expression of cytolysis-related genes, including Ncr1, Gzma, Gzmb, Prf1, and Fgl2 (Figure 4G; Figure 4—figure supplement 2, C and D), indicating the strong target-killing ability of this cluster.
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: There is a significant reduction in Prf1 high cNK cell cluster in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Although this cluster is present in both Prdm1 cko and Prdm1+/+ mice, there is a significant reduction in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 4F), indicating the importance of Prdm1 in maintaining this group of cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data showing cluster proportions in Figure 4F.

claim: GO analysis revealed the enrichment signatures of cytolysis, response to virus, and lymphocyte-mediated immunity in the genes upregulated in Prf1 high cNK cell cluster.
source: GO analysis further revealed the enrichment signatures of cytolysis, response to virus, and lymphocyte-mediated immunity in the genes upregulated in Prf1 high cNK cell cluster, further confirming the cytotoxic effects of this cluster (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by GO analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: The predominant majority (92.98%) of Junb high liver cNK cells are derived from Prdm1 cko mice, with less than ten percent (7.02%) originating from Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: The predominant majority (92.98%) of Junb high liver cNK cells are derived from Prdm1 cko mice, with less than ten percent (7.02%) originating from Prdm1+/+ mice (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data showing cluster composition in Figure 4F.

claim: Many signal transduction elements, gene expression regulator, and transcriptional factors, such as Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Nr4a1/2/3, Batf3, Fos, Fosb, Tcf7, and Kit were upregulated in the Junb high liver cNK cells.
source: Many signal transduction elements, gene expression regulator, and transcriptional factors, such as Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Nr4a1/2/3, Batf3, Fos, Fosb, Tcf7, and Kit were upregulated in the Junb high liver cNK cells (Figure 4G; Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The expression of cytotoxicity related genes, such as Gzmb and Prf1, in Junb high cluster was lower than other cNK cell clusters.
source: The expression of cytotoxicity related genes, such as Gzmb and Prf1, in Junb high cluster was lower than other cNK cell clusters (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: GO analysis showed that genes upregulated in Junb high liver cNK cells enriched in cell differentiation, cell activation, and transcriptional regulation.
source: GO analysis showed that genes upregulated in Junb high liver cNK cells enriched in cell differentiation, cell activation, and transcriptional regulation (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by GO analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: GSEA indicates that the NF-kappa B, IL-17, MAPK, and TNF signaling pathways were upregulated in Junb high cNK cell cluster.
source: GSEA indicates that the NF-kappa B, IL-17, MAPK, and TNF signaling pathways were upregulated in this clusters (Figure 4, I-L).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4I-L.

claim: GSEA showed that mitochondrial related pathways, such as mitochondrial protein, oxidative phosphorylation, and respiratory electron transport chain were suppressed in Junb high cNK cell cluster.
source: GSEA also showed that mitochondrial related pathways, such as mitochondrial protein, oxidative phosphorylation, and respiratory electron transport chain were suppressed in Junb high cNK cell cluster (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, E-G).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E-G.

claim: The Cxcr3 high cNK cell cluster was characterized with high expression of Cxcr3, Ccr2, and some genes encoding ribosomal subunits such as Rps7.
source: The Cxcr3 high cNK cell cluster was characterized with high expression of Cxcr3, Ccr2, and some genes encoding ribosomal subunits such as Rps7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Expression of tissue-resident markers Cd69 was highly expressed in Cxcr3 high cNK cluster.
source: Expression of tissue-resident markers Cd69 was also highly expressed in this clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Cxcr3 high cNK clusters have the highest ILC1 signature score among all cNK clusters.
source: Cxcr3 high cNK clusters have the highest score among all cNK clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 2H), indicating the similarity with liver ILC1s.
evidence: The claim is supported by module score analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2H.

claim: The remarkably decreased proportion of Cxcr3 high cNK cell cluster in Prdm1 cko mice emphasized the critical role of Prdm1 in maintaining this cluster of liver cNK cells.
source: The remarkably decreased proportion of Cxcr3 high cNK cell cluster in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 4F) emphasized the critical role of Prdm1 in maintaining this cluster of liver cNK cells, consistent with the flow cytometry result that showed an increase in the number of NK cells in the bone marrow and a decrease in NK cells in peripheral tissues (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data showing cluster proportions in Figure 4F and flow cytometry data in Figure 1G.

claim: Three clusters of ILC1s were identified from liver ILC1s, comprising 'Il7r high', 'Klra high', and 'Gzmb high' ILC1s.
source: Three clusters of ILC1s were identified from liver ILC1s (Figure 5A), comprising 'Il7r high', 'Klra high', and 'Gzmb high' ILC1s.
evidence: The claim describes the identification of ILC1 subclusters from scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko ILC1s seemed to co-cluster largely and have minor difference within the proportion of clusters.
source: Prdm1+/+ and Prdm1 cko ILC1s seemed to co-cluster largely and have minor difference within the proportion of clusters (Figure 5, B and C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B, C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Both Gzma and Gzmb expression were downregulated, and Junb was upregulated, in Prdm1 cko mice derived cNK cells and ILC1s compared to those from Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Additionally, both Gzma and Gzmb expression were downregulated, and Junb was upregulated, in Prdm1 cko mice derived cNK cells and ILC1s compared to those from Prdm1+/+ mice (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The Il7r high ILC1s cluster was distinguishable from other ILC1 clusters by its high expression of Il7r, Il18r1 (IL18RA), and Ifng (IFN-γ).
source: The Il7r high ILC1s cluster was distinguishable from other ILC1 clusters by its high expression of Il7r, Il18r1 (IL18RA), and Ifng (IFN-γ) (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: GSEA and GO analysis showed that IL-17, NF-kappa B, TNF, MAPK signaling pathway and T cell differentiation were activated in the Il7r high ILC1 cluster.
source: GSEA and GO analysis showed that IL-17, NF-kappa B, TNF, MAPK signaling pathway and T cell differentiation were activated in the Il7r high ILC1 cluster (Figure 5, F-H; Figure 5—figure supplement 1, E-G).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA and GO analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5F-H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E-G.

claim: Several ILC3 signature genes, such as Rora, Tmem176a, and Tmem176b, highly expressed in Il7r high ILC1 cluster.
source: Several ILC3 signature genes, such as Rora, Tmem176a, and Tmem176b (Robinette et al., 2015), highly expressed in this cluster (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D with citation to ILC3 signature genes.

claim: There was an elevated proportion of Klra high ILC1s in Prdm1 cko ILC1s (39.7%) compared to Prdm1+/+ ILC1s (28.1%).
source: Notably, there was an elevated proportion of Klra high ILC1s in Prdm1 cko ILC1s (39.7%) compared to Prdm1+/+ ILC1 s (28.1%; Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data showing cluster proportions in Figure 5C.

claim: Liver Ly49E+ ILC1s have been identified as possessing greater cytotoxic potential and a more robust viral response compared to liver Ly49E- ILC1s.
source: Liver Ly49E+ ILC1s have been identified as possessing greater cytotoxic potential and a more robust viral response compared to liver Ly49E- ILC1s (Chen et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2022.

claim: The Klra high cluster exhibited notably high expression of Ccl5.
source: The Klra high cluster exhibited notably high expression of Ccl5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The expression of Ccl5 was reduced in the Klra high cluster of Prdm1 cko ILC1s compared to Prdm1+/+ ILC1s.
source: The expression of Ccl5 was reduced in the Klra high cluster of Prdm1 cko ILC1s compared to Prdm1+/+ ILC1 s (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), which could potentially have a detrimental impact on the ability of Klra high ILC1s to develop a connection between innate and adaptive immune responses.
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The Gzmb high ILC1 cluster was identified according to the high expression of Gzma, Gzmb, and Fgl2 compared to other ILC1 clusters.
source: The Gzmb high ILC1 cluster was identified according to the high expression of Gzma, Gzmb, and Fgl2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D) compared to other ILC1 clusters.
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: GO analysis revealed the enrichment in cytolysis and stimulus-response capacity of the Gzmb high ILC1 cluster.
source: GO analysis also revealed the enrichment in cytolysis and stimulus-response capacity (Figure 5H) of the Gzmb high ILC1 cluster.
evidence: The claim is supported by GO analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The proportion of the Gzmb high cluster among liver ILC1s exhibited a considerable reduction in Prdm1 cko mice compared to Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Consistent with the Prf1 high cNK cell cluster, the proportion of the Gzmb high cluster among liver ILC1s exhibited a considerable reduction in Prdm1 cko mice compared to Prdm1+/+ mice, and the expression of Gzma also downregulated in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: 17 DEGs are regulated by Prdm1 among liver cNK cells, splenic cNK cells, and liver ILC1s.
source: Through the integration of the bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq data, we identified 17 DEGs that are regulated by Prdm1 among liver cNK cells, splenic cNK cells, and liver ILC1s.
evidence: The claim is supported by integration of bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq data.

claim: Batf3, Junb, Tcf7, and Nfkb1 was upregulated, whereas Gzmb, Prf1, and Fgl2 downregulated, in both Prdm1 cko liver and splenic cNK cells.
source: Batf3, Junb, Tcf7, and Nfkb1 was upregulated, whereas Gzmb, Prf1, and Fgl2 downregulated, in both Prdm1 cko liver and splenic cNK cells (Figure 5J).
evidence: The claim is supported by integrated analysis shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Cxcr6 was downregulated in liver ILC1s and splenic cNK cells in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Cxcr6 was downregulated in liver ILC1s and splenic cNK cells in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 5J).
evidence: The claim is supported by integrated analysis shown in Figure 5J.

claim: A notable negative correlation was observed between the expression levels of Prdm1 and Batf3 in spleen NK cells based on published sequencing data.
source: Based on the sequencing data published by Flommersfeld et al. (GSE180978), a notable negative correlation was observed between the expression levels of Prdm1 and Batf3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: The claim is supported by reanalysis of published data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2I.

claim: Following the knockout of Hobit, the DEGs were primarily identified within ILC1s, whereas after the knockout of Prdm1, a greater number of DEGs were observed in cNK cells.
source: Following the knockout of Hobit, the DEGs were primarily identified within ILC1s. Conversely, after the knockout of Prdm1, a greater number of DEGs were observed in cNK cells. This indicates that Prdm1 likely possesses a broader range of target genes within cNK cells, whereas Hobit appears to have a more pronounced impact on gene expression within ILC1s (Figure 5—figure supplement 2, C-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of Prdm1 and Hobit knockout scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C-F.

claim: Genes such as Junb, Fosb, Tcf7, Kit, Gzmb, Prf1, and Cxcr6 were simultaneously upregulated or downregulated in both Prdm1 cko and HobitKO liver cNK cells or ILC1s.
source: Specifically, genes such as Junb, Fosb, Tcf7, Kit, Gzmb, Prf1, and Cxcr6 were simultaneously upregulated or downregulated in both Prdm1 cko and HobitKO liver cNK cells or ILC1s, indicating the similar regulatory networks of Prdm1 and Hobit.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of DEGs between Prdm1 and Hobit knockout models.

claim: Following the deletion of Prdm1 in Group 1 ILCs, there is a significant increase in both the proportion and number of macrophages in the liver.
source: Our analysis showed that, following the deletion of Prdm1 in Group 1 ILCs, there is a significant increase in both the proportion and number of macrophages in the liver (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: There is a significant decrease in the interaction number and interaction strength between liver group 1 ILCs and macrophages (~1.5 fold) in Prdm1 cko mice.
source: Although the quantity of macrophages significantly increases in Prdm1 cko mice, there is a significant decrease in the interaction number and interaction strength between liver group 1 ILCs and macrophages (~1.5 fold) in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 6, F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by CellChat analysis shown in Figure 6F and G.

claim: The reduction of interaction mostly occurred in the cross-talk of ILC1-MDM and ILC1-KC, whereas no difference was observed in cNK-MDM and cNK-KC interaction.
source: The reduction of interaction mostly occurred in the cross-talk of ILC1-MDM and ILC1-KC, whereas no difference was observed in cNK-MDM and cNK-KC interaction (Figure 6—figure supplement 2, A-H).
evidence: The claim is supported by CellChat analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-H.

claim: A reduction in the interaction of ligand-receptor, such as Mif-CD74, Cxcl16-Cxcr6, and Cxcl10-Cxcr3 was observed in Prdm1 cko mice compared to Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: A reduction in the interaction of ligand-receptor, such as Mif-CD74, Cxcl16-Cxcr6, and Cxcl10-Cxcr3 was observed in Prdm1 cko mice compared to Prdm1+/+ mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by CellChat analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: The information flow of CXCL and MIF pathways significantly decreased in Prdm1 cko mice compared to Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: Compared to Prdm1+/+ mice, the information flow of CXCL and MIF pathways significantly decreased in Prdm1 cko mice (Figure 6, H and I; Figure 6—figure supplement 2, B, D, F, and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by CellChat analysis shown in Figure 6H, I and Figure 6—figure supplement 2B, D, F, and H.

claim: A substantial decrease in MFIs of MitoTracker was observed in Prdm1 cko splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells, and liver ILC1s when compared to their Prdm1+/+ counterparts.
source: A substantial decrease in MFIs of MitoTracker was observed in Prdm1 cko splenic cNK cells, liver cNK cells, and liver ILC1s when compared to their Prdm1+/+ counterparts (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of mitochondrial mass shown in Figure 7A.

claim: There was no significant difference in MitoSOX and TMRM between Prdm1 cko and Prdm1+/+ mice.
source: There was no significant difference in MitoSOX and TMRM between Prdm1 cko and Prdm1+/+ mice (Figure 7, B and C), which suggested that the ATP synthesize capacity was minimally affected by Prdm1.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: The number of both cNK cells and ILC1s have significant decreased in tumor-bearing liver of Prdm1 cko mice.
source: The proportion changes of cNK cells and ILC1s in Prdm1 cko mice was similar with the no tumor-burden condition, while the number of both cNK cells and ILC1s have significant decreased in tumor-bearing liver (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data from tumor-bearing mice shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Significant deceased of IFN-γ+ cells were observed in Prdm1 cko mice liver cNK cells and ILC1s under the combinate stimulation of IL-12/IL-18 in tumor-bearing mice.
source: Compared with Prdm1+/+ mice, significant deceased of IFN-γ+ cells were observed in Prdm1 cko mice liver cNK cells and ILC1s under the combinate stimulation of IL-12/IL-18 (Figure 7E; Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), which was more remarkable in liver ILC1s.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data from tumor-bearing mice shown in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Group 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) comprise conventional natural killer (cNK) cells and type 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILC1s).
source: Group 1 ILCs consist of cNK cells and ILC1s (Spits et al., 2013; Peng et al., 2013), with distinct developmental trajectories and effect molecules (Bai et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Spits et al., 2013 and Peng et al., 2013.

claim: Both cNK cells and ILC1s play indispensable roles in combatting viral infections, maintaining local immune homeostasis, eradicating malignant transformed cells, and fostering cross-talk with adaptive immunity.
source: Both cNK cells and ILC1s play indispensable roles in combatting viral infections (Weizman et al., 2017), maintaining local immune homeostasis (Schuster et al., 2014), eradicating malignant transformed cells (Ducimetière et al., 2021), and fostering cross-talk with adaptive immunity (Fumagalli et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations describing the functions of group 1 ILCs.

claim: cNK cells demonstrate potent cellular cytotoxicity, facilitating direct elimination of target cells.
source: cNK cells demonstrate potent cellular cytotoxicity, facilitating direct elimination of target cells (Kiessling et al., 1975).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kiessling et al., 1975.

claim: A defining attribute of ILC1s is their predominant cytokine-mediated functions, with limited cellular killing capacity.
source: On the contrary, a defining attribute of ILC1s is their predominant cytokine-mediated functions, with limited cellular killing capacity (Nabekura et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Nabekura et al., 2020.

claim: In a state of homeostasis, liver group 1 ILCs can be discriminated into cNK cells and ILC1s by the differential expression of CD49a and CD49b: cNK cells are marked by the expression of CD49b, while liver ILC1s exhibit a distinctive positivity for CD49a.
source: In a state of homeostasis, liver group 1 ILCs (CD45+CD3-NK1.1+NKp46+) can be discriminated into cNK cells and ILC1s by the differential expression of CD49a and CD49b (Peng et al., 2013): cNK cells are marked by the expression of CD49b, while liver ILC1s exhibit a distinctive positivity for CD49a.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Peng et al., 2013.

claim: TRAIL is expressed on liver ILC1s, but not on cNK cells.
source: Tumor Necrosis Factor Related Apoptosis Inducing Ligand (TRAIL) is also expressed on liver ILC1s, but not on cNK cells (Takeda et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Takeda et al., 2001.

claim: Transcriptional factors such as T-bet, Nfil3, PLZF, and ID2 are required for cNK cells and liver ILC1s development or generation of their progenitors.
source: Transcriptional factors (TFs) such as T-bet, Nfil3, PLZF, and ID2 are required for cNK cells and liver ILC1s development or generation of their progenitors (Townsend et al., 2004; Yokota et al., 1999; Gascoyne et al., 2009; Constantinides et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations describing transcription factors required for group 1 ILC development.

claim: Eomes is considered to be necessary for NK cell maturation, but not for ILC1s.
source: Eomes is considered to be necessary for NK cell maturation, but not for ILC1s (Gordon et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gordon et al., 2012.

claim: Deficiency of Hobit results in the depletion of ILC1s, while only leaving little impact on liver NK cells.
source: On the contrary, deficiency of Hobit results in the depletion of ILC1s, while only leaving little impact on liver NK cells (Mackay et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Mackay et al., 2016.

claim: Clinical data showed that liver tumors with a higher infiltration of NK cells are associated with a better prognosis.
source: Clinical data showed that liver tumors with a higher infiltration of NK cells are associated with a better prognosis (Nersesian et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Nersesian et al., 2021.

claim: Decreased NK cell activity is closely correlated with the malignancy of liver tumors and represents a significant risk factor for recurrence.
source: Decreased NK cell activity is closely correlated with the malignancy of liver tumors and represents a significant risk factor for recurrence (Lee et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2021.

claim: The tumor microenvironment orchestrates the transformation of cNK cells into ILC1s in a TGF-β-dependent manner, resulting in their diminished capacity to control tumor growth and metastasis.
source: The tumor microenvironment orchestrates the transformation of cNK cells into ILC1s in a TGF-β-dependent manner, resulting in their diminished capacity to control tumor growth and metastasis. This process ultimately promotes tumor immunoevasion (Gao et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gao et al., 2017.

claim: The primary function of ILC1 is to suppress the seeding of metastatic tumor cells in liver tissue.
source: However, researches also revealed that, distinct from directly inhibiting tumor growth, the primary function of ILC1 is to suppress the seeding of metastatic tumor cells in liver tissue (Ducimetière et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Ducimetière et al., 2021.

claim: Smad4 promotes the shift in balance from cNK cells towards ILC1 in a TGF-beta-independent pathway, and simultaneously, it positively regulates the expression of Prdm1.
source: Our research team, along with others, has observed that one of the transcription factor in TGF-β pathway, Smad4, promotes the shift in balance from cNK cells towards ILC1 in a TGF-beta-independent pathway, and simultaneously, it positively regulates the expression of another transcription factor, PR domain 1 (Prdm1/Blimp1; Wang et al., 2018; Cortez et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2018 and Cortez et al., 2017.

claim: Prdm1 plays a crucial role in the differentiation of B cells into plasma cells and the homeostasis of T cells.
source: Prdm1 plays a crucial role in the differentiation of B cells into plasma cells and the homeostasis of T cells (Keller and Maniatis, 1991; Kallies et al., 2006; Martins et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Keller and Maniatis, 1991; Kallies et al., 2006; Martins et al., 2006.

claim: The expression of Prdm1 in NK cells is independent of B-cell lymphoma 6 (Bcl-6) and Interferon Regulatory actor 4 (IRF4) but relies on T-bet.
source: The function and regulatory network of Prdm1 in NK cells is distinct from B cells and T cells, for its expression is independent of B-cell lymphoma 6 (Bcl-6) and Interferon Regulatory actor 4 (IRF4) but relies on T-bet.
evidence: The claim describes the distinct regulatory mechanism of Prdm1 in NK cells.

claim: In a study that identified Prdm1 as an essential transcriptional factor for NK cell maturation, no significant difference was observed in IFN-γ production or cytotoxicity between Prdm1-deficient and wild-type NK cells.
source: In the study that identified Prdm1 as an essential transcriptional factor for NK cell maturation (Kallies et al., 2011), no significant difference was observed in IFN-γ production or cytotoxicity between Prdm1-deficient and wild-type NK cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kallies et al., 2011.

claim: Prdm1 expression is dependent on IL-15 in immature NK cells and can be further upregulated by IL-12 or IL-21.
source: Although Prdm1 expression is dependent on IL-15 in immature NK cells and can be further upregulated by IL-12 or IL-21, it plays a role in downregulating the expression of certain cytokine receptors, such as CD25 (IL-2Rα), consequently diminishing the responsiveness of NK cells to IL-2 (Akman et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Akman et al., 2021.

claim: Some studies suggested that Prdm1 suppressed the secretion of IFN-γ in NK cells.
source: Notably, some studies even suggested that Prdm1 suppressed the secretion of IFN-γ in NK cells (Smith et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Smith et al., 2010.
